passage:
Dear Vijay,

Remember I told you about my Saturday coding classes for kids? It was great till the half-yearly results. My maths went from 78 to 54. That scared me.

So I sat down with Mummy and Papa and did what you once suggested: set a cap. Now it's six hours a week, maximum. Saturday morning and Wednesday evening, and that's it, even if more parents ask.

And the big one: no classes at all in exam months. February, March and September are blocked on the calendar in red. The parents of my students already know.

Papa also made me write one line: "If any test goes below 65, the gig pauses for a month." We all signed it, a bit jokingly.

It's been six weeks. My maths is back to 71. And oddly, I enjoy the classes more now that they don't eat my whole week.

Vaibhav

qa.q: What is Vaibhav's weekly hour cap?
How did Vaibhav feel when maths dropped from 78 to 54?
qa.a: Vaibhav felt scared and worried, which pushed the change.

qa.q: What else could Vaibhav add to the plan?
qa.a: Vaibhav could review the cap with Mummy and Papa each term, adjusting if school pressure grows.

qa.q: How might the parents of Vaibhav's students see the new limits?
qa.a: They may be a little disappointed about fewer slots, but reassured that the classes are planned and the exam-month break is known in advance.

passage:
So you want to take on more mehendi bookings, Hansa? Let me tell you what happened to me first.

I'm Himani. Last wedding season I said yes to everything. Three brides a week, sometimes on school days. My chemistry marks fell from the eighties to the fifties. I was designing on my palms in class, half asleep.

After that report card, my mother and I sat down with my appointments diary. We agreed: six hours a week, maximum. Sundays and one evening only. And the months of my board exams, February and March, completely blocked. Nothing. Not even for aunties who beg.

We also agreed that if my marks dip again, I pause for a month. No arguing.

It was hard to say no at first. A few families were annoyed. But my marks came back up, and honestly, I do better mehendi when I'm not exhausted. So set your limits first. Then say yes.

qa.a: February and March, the months of the board exams.

qa.q: How did Himani feel during the busy wedding season?
qa.a: Himani felt exhausted, half asleep in class, and later worried by the falling marks.

qa.q: What else should Hansa think about before taking more bookings?
qa.a: Hansa could agree on limits with a parent first, like weekly hours and exam months off, before saying yes to anyone.

qa.q: How did the new limits look to the families who wanted bookings?
qa.a: A few families were annoyed at first, since they were used to Himani saying yes to everything.

grounding: A spoken account of a student who, after a dip in marks, caps gig hours each week, blocks exam months and agrees with a parent on when to pause.
